html:
The Klallam, or S'Klallam, are a Coast Salish people of the northern Olympic Peninsula in Washington, along the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Their language is close to the North Straits Salish languages of the islands to the north.

They lived from salmon, shellfish, sea mammals and cedar, and travelled by canoe across the strait to Vancouver Island. In 1855 they signed the Treaty of Point No Point with the United States. Today there are four Klallam tribes: three in the United States and one band in Canada.

The Lower Elwha Klallam led a long fight to remove two dams on the Elwha River that had blocked salmon since the early 1900s. The dams came down between 2011 and 2014, the largest dam removal in American history. Their western neighbours are the Makah.
